NARRATIVE AND PLANS
TYPE 1 ZONING MAP AMENDMENT APPLICATION

Applicant: 30 North LaSalle Owner, LLC

Property Location: 30 North LaSalle, Chicago, Illinois
Proposed Zoning: DC-16 Downtown Core District
Lot Area: 36,574 square feet

30 North LaSalle Owner, LLC, is the “Applicant” for a Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment for the subject property
located at 30 North LaSalle Street. The Applicant requests a re-zoning from Planned Development Number 596 to
DC-16 Downtown Core District, together with approval of an administrative adjustment to allow alternative
compliance with on-site open space standards, along with all other relief necessary, as allowed by code, for the
attached plans.

The building at 30 North LaSalle Street is a 44-story glass and steel office tower designed by Texas architect
Thomas E, Stanley II and completed in 1974. The building is best known as the structure that replaced the Old
Chicago Stock Exchange, a distinctive Adler and Sullivan-designed commercial building that was demolished in
1972 despite fierce protests from preservationists. Chicago preservationist and architectural photographer Richard
Nickel, known for his tireless efforts to document and preserve the works of Louis Sullivan, lost his life during the
demolition of the Stock Exchange. The demolition of the Stock Exchange served as a galvanizing moment for the
historic preservation movement in Chicago, leading to the formation of the Landmarks Preservation Council (later
Landmarks Illinois) and ushering in a new era of sophisticated, organized, and effective advocacy that would
preserve many of the city’s most architecturally significant buildings.

The Applicant proposes to renovate and adaptively reuse a portion of the existing building to create 349 dwelling
units, residential amenity areas, and residential lobby space. New residential amenity spaces would be provided at
ground level and Level 11. Based on the proposed number of dwelling units, Section 17-4-0410 requires a total of
12,564 sf of on-site open space. The Applicant proposes to provide a total of 11,834 sf of open space, consisting of
9,295 sf of open space at ground level and 2,539 sf of open space on Level 11. A dog run would be provided at
ground level. An exterior terrace would be provided at Level 11. Additional residential amenities include a fitness
center, bocce ball court, studio and party room on Level 11, co-working space on Level 2, and an indoor bike room
at ground level. Bike parking would be provided ata 1:1 ratio for the dwelling units. The remainder of the building
would remain available for renovation and re-occupancy with office and commercial uses. Separate amenity spaces
are proposed for the remaining office areas.

The site is a transit-served location due to its proximity to the Washington/Wells Brown Line CTA Station, the
Monroe Red Line CTA Station, Metra Ogilvie Transportation Center, Union Station, and designated CTA bus line
corridor segments, The DC-16 District does not impose any minimum parking requirements for non-residential
uses, other than hotel and theater uses which are not relevant to this building. The existing building is being
designated as a Chicago Landmark Pursuant to Section 17-10-0102-A, no additional off-street parking or loading
spaces are required for rehabilitation or reuse of an official Chicago Landmark building.

NARRATIVE ZONING ANALYSIS

i. Lot area: 36,574 sf
ii. Total proposed building area: 1,051,041 sf
iii. Proposed FAR: 28.74*

*Note: The existing building consists of 1,049,451 sf of built floor area, equating to a floor area ratio
(FAR) of 28.69. The maximum permitted FAR pursuant to PD 569 is 28.5. To address the existing
nonconforming FAR and the additional 1,590 sf of floor area to be added with development of the project,
the Applicant will separately seek approval of a waiver in bulk standards pursuant to Section 17-14-0202-
L.

The residential project includes removing 1,261 sf of FAR area at Level 2 to create a new double-height
residential lobby on Washington Street. At Level 11, modifications include removing 2,913 sf of FAR area
to create an exterior roof terrace dedicated to the residential program. Also on Level 11, 3,737 sf of
existing mechanical area will be converted to residential amenity program.

The office project would include an increase of 654 sf of FAR area by pushing the storefront at the office
lobby out to the stone columns. This modification would partially restore the historic building condition.
Approximately 1,130 sf of FAR area would be removed at Level 2 to create a double-height lobby, and
approximately 4,563 sf on Level 44 would be removed to create a new double-height lounge space. A new
rooftop amenity space would create 7,149 sf of FAR area, resulting from the conversion of existing
rooffelevation mechanical space.

The total FAR floor area is proposed to be 1,051,041 sf which is within 10% of the existing
nonconforming FAR floor area, less the proposed FAR floor area to be removed.
